(2015). The input is a 224 %224 image, which is passed through a version of the VGG network and even- tually transformed into a representation of size 4096 using a fully connected layer. This contains information about the entire image. This is then reformed into a representation of size 7x7 using another fully connected layer, and the image is upsampled and deconvolved (transposed convolutions without upsampling) in a mirror image of the VGG network. The output is a 224x224x21 representation that gives the output probabilities for the 21 classes at each position.
